description: Flask-based web application implementing a CAPTCHA-protected user registration form. The application uses AES-256 encryption to store CAPTCHA values in encrypted cookies and validates CAPTCHA responses with CSRF protection enabled.

details.authentication: CSRF token required, no user authentication

notes: Application appears to be a security testing benchmark focused on CAPTCHA padding oracle vulnerabilities. The CAPTCHA cookie uses AES encryption but with a hardcoded key visible in the source code. The application generates 14-character CAPTCHA strings but only displays the first 8 characters on the image, requiring users to guess the last 6 characters. CSRF token is properly implemented on the form. Main registration form - GET returns form with CAPTCHA image, POST validates CAPTCHA response. Application uses encrypted cookies for session management and CAPTCHA storage with AES-256-CBC encryption using PKCS7 padding and a hardcoded key.
